Open the map page

1
East-West pipeline hit, Medina region (9 Nov)
Saudi Energy Ministry: an attack caused a limited fire on the pipeline in the Medina region, put out with operations unaffected; exact spot not given (approximate).
2
Missiles intercepted over Riyadh (10 Nov)
The coalition says a ballistic and a cruise missile were downed over Riyadh on 10 Nov, after debris damaged the Aramco Tower on 8 Nov; no output loss reported.
3
14 Hormuz crossings in 48 h (to 8 Nov), 8 dark
Windward counted 11 crossings on 7 Nov (3 tankers) against 84-140 a day pre-war; Kpler put October Hormuz crude at about 10.2 mb/d, 60% of pre-war (area approximate).
4
UAE exports ~4.4 mb/d (9 Nov), up from 3.2
A UAE official says exports are almost 4.4 mb/d vs 3.1-3.2 mb/d before the war, helped by the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline that avoids Hormuz.
5
Tanker on fire 8 nm NW of Khasab (7 Nov)
UKMTO: a tanker caught fire about 8 nm north-west of Khasab on 7 Nov and the crew were evacuated; Iran's navy says another tanker hit a mine in the eastern strait on 8 Nov (unconfirmed).
6
54 ships holding in Gulf (9 Nov), down from 197
straits.live counted 54 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box at 08:30 UTC on 9 Nov, against 97 on 8 Nov and 197 on 4 Nov; AIS coverage varies (area approximate).
7
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 10 Nov 2026

Less oil is leaving the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1-16.6 mb/d of crude across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October, of which only about 10.2 mb/d went through Hormuz itself, about 60% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war level. Traffic through the strait stays very thin (Windward: 14 crossings in the 48 hours to 8 Nov, over half dark), so bypass routes carry over 40% of exports, with the UAE saying its exports have risen to almost 4.4 mb/d via Fujairah. Attacks reached the bypass routes again: the Saudi Energy Ministry said the East-West pipeline was hit in the Medina region on 9 Nov (limited fire, operations unaffected) and missiles were intercepted over Riyadh on 10 Nov. Diplomacy moved too: Trump called the war 'effectively over' militarily after meeting Qatar's prime minister on 9 Nov, and Brent fell almost 6% to about $92.6.
